title: Validation of novel, accelerated and artifact-resistant techniques in whole-body magnetic resonance imaging
summary:
Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) - also known as "nuclear spin" - is a central pillar of modern imaging diagnostics. No other method enables the imaging and diagnostics of a large number of anatomical and physiological processes as well as pathological tissue changes in a comparable way. This broad diagnostic spectrum is created in MRI through a high level of variability in signal acquisition through the use of a wide variety of measurement sequences.
Disadvantages of MRI in scientific and clinical use are the relatively long measurement time and a comparatively high susceptibility to measurement artifacts. Current MRI research is producing methods which promise a significant improvement in robustness and a noticeable acceleration of MRI examinations. These procedures use optimized methods of data acquisition on the one hand, and novel data processing methods on the other. In both cases, an influence on the information content of the generated images is to be expected.
The aim of this research project is to assess novel, accelerated and robust MRI techniques with regard to their technical maturity, their clinical applicability and their diagnostic information content.
For this purpose, MRI measurements should be carried out on healthy test subjects and on suitable patient groups.
conditions: Healthy volunteers and patients are examined. A wide variety of diseases / health problems are examined in patients. The most important criterion is a clinically indicated MRI examination.

interventions.name: In healthy subjects: Evaluation of MRI sequences and sequence order with regard to parameterization of the sequences, image quality and potential clinical application.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Healthy subjects:
- Healthy adults (male or female),
- Age: 18-60 years,
- Letter of acceptance (informed consent).

Patients:
- male and female patients,
- Age: 18-85 years,
- Letter of acceptance (informed consent),
- Carrying out a clinically indicated MRI examination as part of clinical routine (no study-related intervention).
Exclusion criteria:
Healthy subjects:
- MRI contraindications,
- pregnancy / lactation,
- claustrophobia,
- Lack of consent to the communication of incidental findings.

Patients:
- MRI contraindications,
- pregnancy / lactation,
- Claustrophobia.
